params.body:
## What

`AUTH_REFUSAL` in `packages/core/models.mjs` now also matches the CLI's newest refusal:

> Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code

## Why

On 14 October one of the two Max logins answered every call with that sentence. It matched none of the earlier wordings, so `parseCliResult` threw a generic `LLM error`:

- the login was never marked down, so the next account was never asked;
- no refusal was recorded, so the monitor stayed on "Everything under control";
- the support judge (`judge-support.mjs`, hourly from cron) wrote no verdict from 12:45 to 15:45 UTC: three batches failed per insight, and the run stopped after three insights.

With the match, the call takes the same path as every other refused login: the account is marked down, the next one answers, the refusal shows up in the monitor, and the probe re-tests the login every five minutes until it answers again.

## Tests

- `test/auth-refusal.test.mjs` gets the new wording in its list of refusals.
- The full suite gives 1190 of 1196; the 6 failures are the known report-render tests that need Chromium, unchanged.
params.title: Models: treat a disabled subscription as a refused login
